correctness.rationale: Parseval gives the exact shared squared coefficient budget M²−1. The two-channel Cauchy–Schwarz chord kernel has norm sqrt(2S(r)), producing the global lower Lipschitz bound, which is positive exactly below the unique root. The geometric-decay Riesz representer meets the L² norm and approaches tangential equality for every subcritical r. At the root an explicit norm-attaining map has both Wirtinger derivatives 1/2 and vanishing Jacobian; Lewy excludes injectivity on larger disks. M=1 forces the identity. Checker confirms 4 rational partial sums, 7 root/extremal cases and 3 tangential profiles; finite checks only supplement analytic proof.

value.rationale: The p=2 case is a natural Hilbertian member of the sharp 1<p<infinity Landau problem explicitly raised by arXiv:2604.14217v1, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice. The result gives the exact worst-case radius for all norm budgets M, a sharp continuous Euclidean co-Lipschitz profile, and concrete norm-attaining extremals where the Jacobian degenerates. It quantifies full reconstruction/injectivity stability, a substantive invariant not supplied by known sufficient coefficient bounds. No claim about the independent schlicht-disk invariant is made.
